provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The output canvas is h*h by w*w. The input acts as its own map: every cell holding the rarest colour becomes a block containing a full copy of the input, placed at block position (r, c). This mechanism is already equivariant under all D4 transforms. Rotating or reflecting the input moves each selector cell and its block together, so the emitted program stamps directly in visible coordinates and needs no direction constants. Under the palette, the only fixed colour role is the empty background, original 0, so the canvas is filled with palette[0]. The rarest colour is unique by construction. As a defensive tie-break, the program picks the tied colour whose original (pre-palette) index is smallest, which mirrors the archived argmin-over-sorted-values behaviour in original colour space.
draft_notes.limitations: This assumes, as the generator guarantees, that the input is a 3x3 grid with a unique least-frequent colour. The program also handles general h x w inputs with an h*h x w*w output, matching the archived solver. The background is assumed to be the palette image of original colour 0. The fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule, and no contradictions were found. None of this has been run or tested.

recertification_note: Native batch F recertified this unchanged factory on a widened constructor: input height and width are sampled independently in 2..5 (output H*H x W*W <= 25x25). Legacy nominal 2..4-colour subset, not all required (1..4 used colours, monochrome included), unique least frequent colour. The draft notes below were written for the legacy 3x3 domain and are kept verbatim. The factory already handled general H x W inputs.
